title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Support Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Operational playbook for Developer Experience docs: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and canonical fixes for top support issues.
body:
Overview
--------
This document defines standards, templates, and operating procedures for the Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation surface: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the canonical top-support-issues / fixes list. The goal is to keep user-facing docs consistent, discoverable, and low-friction for developers integrating Redwood Inference.

Intended audience
- DevEx engineers and technical writers
- SDK maintainers and owners
- Solutions engineers and support engineers
- Product and developer advocates

Outcomes
- Reusable quickstarts and templates that reduce time-to-first-success for customers
- High-quality, tested SDK guides and API examples that map to supported runtime behaviors
- Clear operating procedures for doc updates, release syncs, and incident-driven doc fixes
- Single source of truth for top support issues with canonical diagnostics and fixes

1) Documentation types & when to use them
------------------------------------------------
- SDK Guide: Full reference + idiomatic examples for each SDK (Python, TypeScript, Go). Use for API reference, auth, pagination, streaming, and advanced usage (tool calls, structured outputs).
- Quickstart: Minimal steps to make your first request and get a meaningful response. Use for onboarding and marketing pages.
- Template: Reusable snippet of config or code (serverless function, Dockerfile, terraform module). Use for reproducible setup patterns.
- API Example: Short, copy-paste examples that demonstrate core parameters and response shapes. Keep these < 30 lines.
- Docs Site Ops Page: Operational runbook for publishing workflow, rollbacks, and auditing. Use for on-call and doc maintainers.
- Support Playbook: Curated list of top reported issues and canonical fixes/calls to action for support agents.

2) File and page naming conventions
------------------------------------------------
- Page slugs and file names should be kebab-case and concise. Example: "python-sdk-quickstart-2027" or "nodejs-streaming-example".
- SDK guides: "sdk-{language}-guide-{year}"
- Quickstarts: "{product}-quickstart-{language}-{year}"
- Templates: "template-{usecase}-{language}"
- API examples: "api-example-{capability}-{language}"

3) SDK guide required sections (template)
------------------------------------------------
Include the following headings in every SDK guide:
- Title and short summary (1-2 lines)
- Quickstart snippet (copy-paste runnable)
- Authentication and configuration (env vars, best practices)
- Full reference of primary client APIs with param examples
- Error handling patterns and retry guidance (idempotency notes)
- Streaming/long-running patterns (if supported)
- Advanced features (tool-calling, structured outputs, function calling)
- Migration notes (breaking changes across versions)
- Compatibility and supported runtimes/versions
- Tests and examples (link to repo snippets)
- Owner and repo links

4) Quickstart & template guidance
------------------------------------------------
- Keep Quickstarts < 10 steps. Aim for time-to-first-success < 5 minutes using only the examples provided.
- Include one runnable example for hosted API and one for Dedicated/Private where flows differ (auth, endpoint).
- Provide a minimal Dockerfile or serverless handler as a template for production readiness.
- For templates that include infrastructure (terraform, helm), provide a small config table listing required variables and defaults.

Example quickstart (Python, hosted)
1. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your environment.
2. Install: pip install redwood-sdk
3. Run: python quickstart.py

quickstart.py
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
resp = client.text.generate(model="redwood-alpha", prompt="Say hello from Redwood!")
print(resp.text)
```

5) API examples style guide
------------------------------------------------
- Keep examples short, tested, and language-idiomatic. Prioritize official SDKs: Python and TypeScript first, then Go and examples for curl.
- Always show:
  - Minimal request
  - Streaming example (if applicable)
  - Error-handling/retry example
  - Example inputs that exercise shapes (e.g., function call payloads)
- Use realistic values for prompts/inputs, but never include customer data.

6) Docs site operating procedures (publishing and rollback)
------------------------------------------------
Publisher role and checklist
- Each doc must have an owner listed on the page. Owners are responsible for accuracy and updates.
- Before publishing: spellcheck, code snippet lint, run local dev server, and validate links.
- Version pinning: include SDK version used in examples. Update during SDK releases.
- Accessibility: add alt text for images and ensure examples have clear labels.

Publishing flow (step-by-step)
1. Create PR against docs repo with doc content and tests (examples run in CI).
2. Assign reviewers from DevEx (minimum 2 reviewers, one owner + one peer).
3. CI must pass lint, linkcheck, and example smoke tests.
4. Merge and verify on staging docs site.
5. Author runs a quick smoke test of 3 canonical quickstarts.
6. Promote to production during low-traffic window or per release cadence.

Rollback procedure
1. If a doc causes regression (broken examples, security issue), create a patch PR labeled "docs: hotfix - rollback".
2. Notify #devex-docs channel and on-call.
3. Revert the merge commit if urgent, then follow the merge flow for the fix.

7) CI requirements for docs changes
------------------------------------------------
- Linting: markdown/static site linter with our ruleset.
- Example smoke tests: run the quickstart examples with a sandbox key in ephemeral environment. Tests must complete in < 60s.
- Link check: 404s fail the build.
- Size check: images > 1MB require approval and justification.

8) Top support issues & canonical fixes (support playbook)
------------------------------------------------
We maintain the top 10 recurring developer-facing issues and exact diagnostic steps + fixes. Keep this list curated and updated monthly. Below are the current canonical entries.

Issue 1: "401 / invalid API key"
- Symptoms: Immediate 401 responses for all calls.
- Diagnostics: Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY set in environment; confirm key has not expired in Console; verify no extra whitespace.
- Canonical fix: Rotate key in Console, update environment, restart process/container. If key rotation fails, escalate to identity team with log bundle.

Issue 2: "Network errors / TLS issues when connecting to Private deployment"
- Symptoms: TLS handshake failures or certificate errors.
- Diagnostics: Check endpoint host/port, confirm root CA in customer's system store, test with curl -v to endpoint, inspect proxy settings.
- Canonical fix: Provide customer's CA bundle installation steps, verify DNS mapping, and advise restart of service. Escalate to eng-private-deployments if certificate mismatch persists.

Issue 3: "Streaming responses cut off"
- Symptoms: Partial responses or connection closes during streaming output.
- Diagnostics: Check client-side read loop, network timeouts, reverse proxy/gateway idle timeouts. Reproduce with our streaming-example client with debug logs.
- Canonical fix: Increase idle timeouts on proxies and clients; ensure keepalive headers; upgrade SDK to latest streaming patch.

Issue 4: "High token latency on shared-hosted"
- Symptoms: Tokens-per-second lower than SLO, bursty tail latencies.
- Diagnostics: Check model routing logs, batching configuration, and current capacity utilization.
- Canonical fix: Suggest customer pin dedicated capacity or tune batching windows; apply temporary throughput policy. Route to eng-sre for mitigation if widespread.

Issue 5: "Model mismatch / unexpected output format"
- Symptoms: Responses missing the expected function call JSON or wrong structured format.
- Diagnostics: Validate request parameters (response_format, function schema), evaluate model version and quantization profile. Run evaluation harness with prompt set.
- Canonical fix: Update request to include the correct function schema and model parameter; if regression detected, file a regression-triage ticket and flag model-onboarding.

(Entries 6-10): Includes issues such as dependency conflicts in SDKs, rate limit errors, region routing mistakes, ambiguous error messages, and incorrect example snippets. Maintain full diagnostic steps in the support-playbook repo.

9) Documentation ownership and SLAs
------------------------------------------------
- Owners must respond to doc-related P1/P2 incidents within 2 business hours.
- Monthly docs health check: owners confirm examples run, links valid, and update labels.
- Quarterly docs review: all top quickstarts and SDK guides are reviewed by product and a DevEx engineer.

10) Metrics and success criteria
------------------------------------------------
Track these metrics to measure docs effectiveness:
- Time-to-first-success (TTFS) for quickstarts (goal < 5 minutes)
- Number of support tickets referencing docs (goal: downward trend)
- Docs site search success rate (click-through for first result > 50%)
- Example smoke test pass rate in CI (goal 100%)

11) Example templates and checklists (appendix)
------------------------------------------------
Publishing checklist (one-liner)
- [ ] Owner set on page
- [ ] Examples tested and pinned to SDK version
- [ ] CI smoke tests passing
- [ ] Reviewer approvals (>=2)
- [ ] Release notes entry (if user-facing change)

Minimal quickstart template
- Title: 1-line summary
- Prereqs: API key, language runtime, CLI or package manager
- Install: copy/paste command(s)
- Run: example command and expected output
- Next steps: link to SDK guide and reference docs

Contact and escalation
- Primary channel: #devex-docs (Slack)
- Pager: Documentation owners are on-call per rotation for major doc incidents
- Escalation: If issue is product or infra, escalate to eng-platform or eng-sre with logs and CI artifacts attached.
